_description:
# Help and flag placement

Where flags may go, which commands differ, help levels and short names.

placement._description: A flag may go anywhere after the name of the level that owns it; a few hand the words after a point on unread.

target._description: Which aos-agent subcommands take the agent as -t NAME or as the last argument.

text._description: Text handed on as it is ends flag reading; after -- nothing is a flag.

help._description: Each level has its own --help; FlagUnknown, ArgumentsBad and CommandUnknown.

short._description: Short names are per command; use separate tokens.

placement:
# A flag goes after its level

A command has levels: the program, its subcommand, the action (`aos-agent`, `ctl`, `stop`). A flag belongs to one level and may go anywhere after that level's name, also after later names and arguments. These are the same:

```sh
aos-agent -d /srv/d ctl stop bob
aos-agent ctl stop bob -d /srv/d
aos-agent ctl stop -t bob
aos-tools add tools/clock --name now
```

This holds for every aos command, the parts in `aos/cli/parts/` too (`aos-json get FILE#/a --str`, `aos-eca-turn /abs/def --one`). Exceptions, where words are handed on as they are: everything after the folder in `aos-exec FOLDER ARGS` goes to that folder's program; `aos-sandbox CONFIG PROG ...` hands PROG and its args on; `aos-json set`, `append` and `merge` take their flags before FILE, because the value may be any word (`aos-json set --str FILE#/a -x`). A word after an argument that looks like a negative number (`-3`) or holds a space stays an argument.
target:
# Naming the agent in aos-agent

`aos-agent ctl` start / stop / sleep / wake / pause / resume / where take the agent as `-t NAME` or as the last argument. say, listen, chat, open, close, watch, tools, llm, system, history and hook take only `-t`. `ctl add / rm / ls / who` take no `-t`. Two different names = `ArgumentsBad`.
text:
# Text ends flag reading

Text that is handed on as it is ends flag reading: everything from the first word of `aos-agent say WORDS`, `history summarize RANGE TEXT`, `history set LINE JSON`, `goal set TEXT`, `aos-mailbox send WHAT`, `aos-clock-register add NAME TEXT` is text, so put flags before it. After `--` nothing is a flag: `aos-daemon-ctl add tools/job -- --verbose`, `aos-agent say -t bob -- -hello`.
help:
# Help levels

Run `aos-agent --help`, then `aos-agent tools --help`, then `aos-agent tools add --help`. Each prints only its own level. Help needs no live daemon or target. Commands with subcommands work the same: `aos-post send --help`, `aos-json set --help`.

A flag nobody in the command knows gives `FlagUnknown`. No subcommand gives `ArgumentsBad` (`aos-post: error: ArgumentsBad missing subcommand`); an unknown subcommand gives `CommandUnknown`.
short:
# Short names

Common default short names are: `-h --help`, `-d --daemon`, `-t --target`, `-j --json`, `-n --name`, `-w --ws`, `-s --stack`, `-f --follow`, `-y --yes`. Each command defines its own short names and may give them different meanings (aos-mailbox `-s` is your own stack; aos-clock-register `-c` is the clock). Only use a short name where that help lists it. `--file`, `--detach` and `--timeout-s` have no short name. `-s`/`-w` are not aliases for the switches in `ctl where`, or the path in `ctl who`.

Use separate tokens: `-t bob`. `-tbob` and `-jf` are unknown flags.
